data.title: Canada Retail Sales Slip After Rising a Sixth Straight Month in June — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart 




  OTTAWA--Canadian spending, which has helped underpin a sluggish economy, stalled last month and snapped a run of rising retail trade through the first half of 2026. 



  The value of retail trade in the country rose a stronger-than-expected 0.6% in June from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 74.28 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of about US$53.87 billion, Statistics Canada said Friday. 



  Yet an early tally of receipts indicates sales in July declined 0.8%, the first drop since the end of 2025. Sales growth in March, April and May was revised slightly higher. 



  The data agency offered no detail with its July estimate, which was based on responses from more than half of retailers surveyed, though it coincides with a fresh spike in fuel costs with the Iran conflict and with lingering worries about the fallout of U.S. tariffs. 



  Analysis of cardholder activity by Royal Bank of Canada, the country's largest lender, showed that consumers continued to spend through what was a challenging quarter, likely drawing on savings or taking on debt amid higher energy costs and weak wage gains. It found purchases of essentials excluding fuel grew for the period, while cardholder spending on discretionary goods recovered after a weak year and a half. 



  "While consumers showed up in June, a weak July flash highlights the risks they face in keeping up momentum amid trade- and war-driven uncertainty," said Shelly Kaushik, senior economist at Bank of Montreal Capital Markets. 



  In volume terms, retail sales rose 1.5% between June and July and were 2.1% higher than a year earlier. With factory and wholesale volumes also up solidly for the month, economists say monthly gross domestic product is tracking stronger than Statistics Canada's earlier estimate of 0.2% growth. 



  Sales in June were up in seven of the nine industry segments the data agency tracks, led by general merchandise stores, which includes super centers, warehouse clubs and the country's few remaining department stores. Compared with the same month last year, nominal sales were up 5.2% overall in June. 



  Consumers also bought more at clothing, accessories, shoe, luggage and leather goods stores during the month. 



  The monthly advance, which was a touch stronger than the 0.4% growth economists had expected, came despite a drag from gasoline stations and fuel vendors where receipts fell for the first time in four months as prices retreated. Stripping out fuel, retail sales in Canada rose 1.2% for the month. 



  Core sales, which exclude fuel as well as motor vehicles and parts, were up a third month running. The sole decrease in core sales was at food and drink retailers, a segment led by supermarkets and other grocery stores. 



  Canada's economy was growing in recent months and industry-level data points to an annualized expansion of 3.4% in the second quarter, which would be the strongest in roughly three years and follows back-to-back quarterly contractions. The housing market and resale activity have picked up after faltering earlier in the year, jobs data shows a recovery in hiring, and surveys indicate businesses are adapting to a trade environment of uncertainty and U.S. tariffs. 



  The Bank of Canada, which has left its policy interest rate unchanged six times in a row and is widely expected to do so again early next month, has noted the economy is showing signs of broadening from a reliance on household and government spending as exports pick up and businesses adapt to U.S. trade policy. 



  "Monthly retail sales data can be very volatile, and even after factoring in July's decline the underlying trend in sales volumes appears to be positive," said Andrew Grantham, senior economist at CIBC Capital Markets. "Looking ahead to 2027, there are reasons to be cautiously optimistic regarding the consumer spending outlook, including the recent improvement seen in the labor market, expanded benefits for lower income households and a reduced drag on disposable incomes from mortgage refinances."

data.title: Our 4-year-old son has $100,000 in his 529 account. Is a bull market a bad time to buy him stocks instead?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'I'd love for our son to be able to attend college without needing to take out student loans'

"We're currently unable to contribute any more to our 401(k)s." (Photo subjects are models.)

Dear Quentin,

My son will turn 4 next month, and we have $100,000 in his 529 college fund. We're wondering whether we should continue contributing to the 529 or start directing more money elsewhere. He also has a brokerage account, but there's only $500 in it.

We're a family of three. We own our home with a 2% mortgage rate; both cars are paid off; we have no debt; we have $430,000 in our 401(k)s, a $100,000 emergency fund, $70,000 in a taxable brokerage account; and we're currently unable to contribute any more to our 401(k)s.

Our overall goal is flexibility, but ideally, I'd love for our son to be able to attend college without needing to take out student loans. Given our situation, would you continue prioritizing the 529, or would you start putting more toward a brokerage account - or somewhere else?

I'd really appreciate any thoughts or perspectives you have. Do we buy stocks in a bull market, or keep contributing to his 529 plan?

The Parent

Don't miss: 'I want safe returns': I'm 73 with $300,000 saved. I'm not interested in the stock market. What should I do?

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

You have a lot of runway before your son goes to college in, say, 14 years.

Dear Parent,

A brokerage account gives you greater control.

At this point in the game, with your solid financial position, you are buying yourself options. The aim is to save one-third to half of your child's college tuition. Happily, 529 plans allow tax-free and penalty-free lifetime rollovers of up to $35,000 into a Roth IRA for the beneficiary, with an annual K-12 withdrawal cap of $20,000.

That goal gives your young son a significant leg up, while allowing you to put enough money aside for your own retirement, and also gives you flexibility when it comes to your son's savings. For all these reasons, given that you have a 529 plan with $100,000, I would probably switch to a brokerage account.

You've maxed out your 401(k), you have an enviable 2% mortgage rate, you have a very generous $100,000 emergency fund, you are free of debt, and you have $100,000 in a 529 account that will hopefully earn between 5% and 7% annually. That's a lot of runway before your son goes to college in, say, 14 years. Those years will creep up fast, but you're on top of it.

As for buying stocks in a bull market, a four-year-old child has a long runway to achieve gains.

Saving one-third of your son's future college expenses usually means you expect to fund his education through a combination of a 529 plan, income during his college years, financial aid, scholarships and, yes, student loans. You don't want to go the latter route and, given that you are debt-free, I have every confidence that you will achieve that.

As for buying stocks in a bull market, a four-year-old child has a long runway to achieve gains. Robert Ross, the founder of TikStocks, wrote a MarketWatch column about this exact topic earlier this week. He cited a study by Dimensional Fund Advisers going back to 1926 showing that a new all-time high in the market occurred every six weeks and, historically, the S&P 500 was higher one year after hitting a record 81% of the time.

"If you're waiting for a 20% crash, the S&P 500 SPX could rally another 30% before it arrives," Ross wrote. "You could correctly predict the next bear market and still end up buying stocks at a higher price than they trade today. And that assumes you have the stomach to buy when the headlines are screaming that things are about to get worse. That's the hidden cost of waiting for the 'perfect' entry."

Don't miss: How much parents actually need to save for college - whether you earn $45,000 or $250,000

There's no one-size-fits-all answer

Where your son chooses to go to college matters. Four-year college costs vary: roughly $124,000 for an in-state public university, $204,000 for an out-of-state public school and $262,000 for a private university. Add $100,000 onto that private-university fee for an Ivy League school. Those costs will rise, along with your son's 529 account, in the intervening years.

Mark Kantrowitz, a student-debt expert and author, writing on Saving for College, says there's no "one-size-fits-all." Your savings target should be based on your child's age, 529 balance, expected investment returns, type of college you're targeting, and how much of the future cost you want to cover.

He notes that Sallie Mae's 2025 "How America Pays for College" publication found that 27% of college costs were actually paid for with scholarships and grants. "For the remaining costs, most parents use a combination of funding sources with 48% of funds coming from savings and income, 23% from loans, and 2% from relatives and friends," he adds.

There's little doubt that college costs will climb. They've risen by more than 900% over the last four decades.

There's little doubt that college costs will still climb. They have risen by more than 900% over the last 40 years, according to JP Morgan, increasing at an average annual rate of about 5.5% to 5.8%. This rate of growth dramatically outpaces normal household expenses, medical care, and even housing over the same multidecade period, it says.

"Student loan debt has surged 343% since 2005, more than three times the pace of college costs, and nearly all recent graduates with college debt (97%) have delayed or abandoned life goals, such as buying a home or starting a family," the report says. "A majority of families (60%) do not use 529 plans."

Robert Ross, citing strong corporate earnings, says the long-term trend is for stocks to keep rising. "Could I get some of these stocks cheaper during the next correction? Absolutely. And I understand why waiting for the perfect entry can feel prudent. Sometimes it is," he wrote. "But history shows that sitting on the sidelines simply because stocks have never been higher can be far more expensive than buying at the top."

The sooner families like you start investing, the more time they have to grow their college fund through the magic of compounding, the JP Morgan report adds. In fact, it says, 83% of 529 plan users make automatic contributions. Keep putting 3% to 5% of your income aside for your child's future, as long as your good fortune and smart financial planning lasts.

Related: 'This is a first-world problem': I can't roll over my $800,000 401(k) from my prior employer. What did I do wrong?

data.title: AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of The Travelers Companies, Inc. and Subsidiaries
data.description:
AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of The Travelers Companies, Inc. and Subsidiaries

AM Best has affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A++ (Superior) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Ratings (Long-Term ICR) of “aa+” (Superior) of the main subsidiaries of The Travelers Companies, Inc. (TRV) (headquartered in New York, NY) [NYSE: TRV], collectively known as Travelers Group (Travelers). In addition, AM Best has affirmed the FSR of A++ (Superior) and the Long-Term ICRs of “aa+” (Superior) of Travelers Casualty and Surety Company of America (TCSA) (Hartford, CT). Concurrently, AM Best has affirmed the FSR of A- (Excellent) and the Long-Term ICR of “a-” (Excellent) of First Floridian Auto and Home Insurance Company (First Floridian) (Tampa, FL).

AM Best also has affirmed the Long-Term ICRs and existing Long-Term Issue Credit Ratings (Long-Term IR) of “a+” (Excellent) of TRV and its two wholly owned downstream holding companies, Travelers Property Casualty Corp. and Travelers Insurance Group Holdings Inc. (both headquartered in Hartford, CT).ll outstanding securities issued by the two downstream holding companies are guaranteed by TRV. At the same time, AM Best has affirmed all other Long-Term IRs and Short-Term Issue Credit Ratings (Short-Term IR) guaranteed by TRV, as well as TRV’s indicative Long-Term IRs. The outlook of these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable.

The ratings of Travelers reflect the group’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as strongest, as well as its very strong operating performance, favorable business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM). The group’s balance sheet strength assessment is supported by the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Additionally, the balance sheet strength assessment reflects the group’s consistent favorable loss reserve development trends, conservative investment portfolio, comprehensive reinsurance programs, as well as the benefit afforded from the additional financial flexibility provided by its publicly traded parent, TRV.

Travelers’ very strong operating performance assessment reflects sustained underwriting and operating profitability over the long-term. In 2025, the group reported $4.1 billion in net underwriting income, the largest in its history. Underwriting results combined with investment income resulted in total net income of $6.5 billion for the year.

The group maintains strong market positions as evidenced by being the fifth largest property/casualty (P/C) insurer in the United States based on 2025 direct premiums written, the seventh largest personal lines writer, and second largest commercial lines writer, per AM Best. In addition, Travelers maintains favorable geographic and product diversification offering a wide variety of P/C coverages in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, Canada, England, Ireland, Guam, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands and the Northern Mariana Islands.

The ratings of TCSA reflect its balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as strongest, as well as its very strong operating performance, favorable business profile and appropriate ERM.

The ratings of First Floridian reflect its balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its marginal operating performance, limited business profile and appropriate ERM. The ratings also reflect the implicit support it receives from its ultimate parent, TRV.

A complete listing of The Travelers Companies, Inc.’s FSRs, Long-Term ICRs and Long- and Short-Term IRs is available.

data.title: Starcloud Raises $250 Million in Series A With Nvidia Backing
data.description:
By Dean Seal 




  Starcloud said it raised $250 million in a series A funding round that saw Nvidia join as a new investor, giving the data center-focused startup a $2.3 billion valuation. 



  The round, led by Manhattan West, also saw participation from existing investors including Benchmark and EQT, along with newcomers such as Cisco Investments and Cedar Capital. 



  Starcloud has now raised $450 million since its founding in 2024. The company is working to deploy data centers into space. 



  The backing from Nvidia comes after Starcloud flew the chipmaker's H100 GPU to orbit on its Starcloud-1 satellite in November 2025. 



  The companies are now working together on Nvidia's Space-1 Vera Rubin Module, an AI hardware system built for the extreme conditions in space. Cooling will be performed by large radiators and components must withstand radiation exposure, they said.

data.title: AEG and Goldenvoice Expand Career Pathways at Just Like Heaven and Head in the Clouds Festivals
data.description:
NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / August 21, 2026 / For most young people, music festivals are places to experience their favorite artists and connect with culture. Increasingly, they are also providing valuable opportunities to explore potential careers behind the scenes of the live entertainment industry.

This summer, more than 40 high school students participated in AEG career exploration events held alongside Goldenvoice's Head in the Clouds and Just Like Heaven festivals at Brookside at the Rose Bowl. The experiences provided students with a firsthand look at the wide range of professions that help bring major live events to life.

Participants explored career opportunities across event production, marketing, operations, food and beverage, stage production and entertainment management while learning how these functions work together to create large scale festival experiences. Guided tours and conversations with industry professionals offered students an insider's perspective on the planning, coordination and execution required to deliver world class events.

Beyond exposing students to career possibilities, the program focused on helping them build practical skills that support future academic and professional success. Through collaborative challenges, students worked in teams to develop original festival concepts and present their ideas to industry leaders, strengthening their communication, team building, critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

The events brought together students from schools and community organizations across the Los Angeles region, creating opportunities for young people to engage directly with professionals and gain insight into an industry that can often feel out of reach. For many participants, the experience provided a clearer understanding of both the educational pathways and professional experiences that can lead to careers in entertainment.

Experiential learning programs like those offered through AEG are becoming increasingly important to Career Technical Education (CTE) programs in high schools. By connecting students with real world environments, professional mentors and hands-on learning opportunities, organizations can help young people make more informed decisions about their futures while building confidence in their ability to pursue ambitious career goals.

As the entertainment industry continues to evolve, developing diverse talent pipelines remains essential to its future success. Through programs like this, AEG and Goldenvoice are helping prepare the next generation of professionals by providing meaningful exposure to the careers, skills and networks that power the live entertainment business.

data.title: Leading With Care: 25 Years of Meaningful Engagement
data.description:
The Boehringer Ingelheim Cares Foundation works alongside partners to address unmet needs across human and animal health and STEM education. Over 25 years, the foundation has expanded its approach-from direct financial and in-kind support toward longer-term partnerships aimed at strengthening communities

NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESS Newswire / August 21, 2026 / In 2001, the Boehringer Ingelheim Cares Foundation (Boehringer Cares) was established to support causes important to the communities where we live and work, pursuing philanthropy that created real impact.

Over the past 25 years, Boehringer Cares has observed a consistent pattern: while direct charitable support is essential to addressing unmet needs, lasting impact depends on partnering with nonprofit organizations that understand and shape the systems influencing health and well-being. This perspective guides Boehringer Cares' approach to partnership and program development, grounded in the belief that meaningful, sustainable change is achieved by working alongside those closest to the challenges. Boehringer Cares channels this focus into its core priority areas, aligning resources and partnerships to drive impact.

Engaging our employees

Across Boehringer Ingelheim, employees actively participate in Boehringer Cares initiatives and generously support its mission through volunteering, financial donations and the matching gifts program.

Community partners, much like Boehringer employees, seek deeper engagement that goes beyond financial support. They seek collaborators who will listen and join them to build capacity and resilience. At the same time, society expects companies to deliver real, measurable impact.

Kristin Segrue, Director, Corporate Social Responsibility and Boehringer Ingelheim Cares Foundation, describes "Leading with Care" about empowering people to drive meaningful change. Boehringer employees exemplify this commitment as volunteers, donors, mentors, and advocates, helping build stronger, more resilient communities together.

"Our programs aim to support people, animals, and communities by bringing together expertise and resources to address unmet community needs."
Kristin Segrue, Director, Corporate Social Responsibility and Boehringer Ingelheim Cares Foundation

Improving access to healthcare

"Leading with Care" means building partnerships to make healthier communities possible where it is needed most. Americares, a nonprofit committed to helping people access health in times of disaster and everyday, is one of our long-term partners in this work.

What began in 2005 as a mobile clinic for uninsured adults in Greater Danbury, Connecticut, became the Boehringer Ingelheim Americares Free Clinic of Danbury in 2009, offering free, high-quality care. In 2016, Boehringer Cares launched a health coaching program that now supports multiple clinics across the state.

Through this alliance, 635 patients received care in 2025, and 11,800 individuals received access to donated Boehringer Ingelheim medicines at no cost.

Advancing disaster preparedness and recovery

The same spirit of care in providing access to healthcare drives Boehringer Cares' disaster preparedness and recovery efforts. By partnering with nonprofits such as Greater Good Charities, Direct Relief, World Central Kitchen, and Americares, the Foundation helps communities anticipate and prepare for disasters.

To strengthen recovery and build long-term resilience, Boehringer Cares prepositions medicine and supplies, ensures rapid response when disasters occur, and remains engaged throughout the rebuilding process. For example, during Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024, more than USD 2 million in products were provided, reaching over 8,000 people and animals.

Boehringer Cares amplifies employee generosity through its matching gift programs, which may match donations at a 2:1 ratio, contributing up to double the original amount to eligible organizations.

  • Since 2023, products valued at more than USD 500M have reached tens of thousands of people and animals, including during Hurricanes Helene and Milton in 2024.

Enhancing STEM education

Many students in under-resourced schools lack access to science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) education programs. They have fewer opportunities to explore hands-on science, fewer role models, and fewer pathways to STEM careers. Boehringer Cares works to close these gaps by supporting the next generation of scientists, innovators and leaders, not just to succeed in STEM, but also to serve their communities.

Since 2009, employees have mentored students through the Connecticut Invention Convention, an education nonprofit that brings innovation and entrepreneurship programs to more than 12,000 young learners annually. STEM Day, launched in 2024 and continued in 2025, engaging high school students through informational sessions, connections with Boehringer employees, hands-on activities, and facility tours. Through STEM education, mentorship, and real-world experiences, Boehringer Cares helps young people see themselves as future healthcare providers and innovators.

Strengthening animal health by championing veterinary well-being

The veterinary field also faces many challenges, including practitioner burnout, workforce shortages, and increasing barriers to care in underserved areas. In response, Boehringer Cares has committed more than USD 2.5 million in 2025 and is investing in partnerships with organizations such as Not One More Vet, National Agriculture in the Classroom, American Association of Bovine Practitioners Foundation, the Farm Journal Foundation, and the University of Georgia.

These strategic partnerships support those who care for animals, nurture the next generation of veterinarians, and expand veterinary care in rural and urban areas. These efforts address critical gaps to ensure the profession remains strong, supported, and prepared for future needs.


Students from Universidad de Puerto Rico gain hands-on veterinary experience while helping expand access to animal care in underserved communities.

Why lead with care?

25 years of learning and commitment have demonstrated that change often begins in the gaps where systems fall short, where people are overlooked, and where needs go unmet.

Boehringer Cares' role is to identify those gaps and help fill them. Together with partners, employees, and communities, Boehringer Cares strives to create solutions for our communities. By leading with care, the foundation works toward building stronger, healthier, and more resilient communities through long-term commitments to its partners and the people they serve.

Learn more about Boehringer Ingelheim Cares Foundation, its mission, initiatives, and partners.

data.title: Sentinel Net Lease Announces Final Closing of Sentinel Opportunity Fund I
data.description:
$101 million portfolio closes with 100% occupancy, and a 10.4-year weighted average lease term

LAS VEGAS, NV / ACCESS Newswire / August 21, 2026 / Sentinel Net Lease today announced the final closing of Sentinel Opportunity Fund I, the firm's inaugural commingled investment fund, following the acquisition of a diversified portfolio of single-tenant office, industrial, and retail properties across the United States.

At closing, the portfolio consisted of 10 stabilized properties representing approximately $101 million in property value and more than 762,000 rentable square feet. The portfolio was 100 percent occupied, with a 10.4-year weighted average remaining lease term and projected 2026 net distributions of 8.7 percent.

Tenants include Abbott Laboratories, Bio-Techne, Merative, and Quantum Corporation in healthcare and technology. V3 Engineering and Knight Energy Services operate in infrastructure and energy. Consumer and retail tenants include Juice Plus+ and LA Fitness.

ABBOTT LABORATORIES - WAUKEGAN, IL

Properties are located in Illinois, Colorado, Tennessee, Ohio, North Carolina, Wisconsin, Louisiana, and North Dakota.

The Fund's final acquisition was the Knight Energy Services industrial portfolio, comprising two facilities in Broussard, Louisiana, and Williston, North Dakota, each leased under long-term absolute triple-net structures.

"Sentinel Opportunity Fund I represents the disciplined investment approach our firm has followed since inception," said Dennis Cisterna, Co-Founder and Chief Investment Officer of Sentinel Net Lease. "Every acquisition was evaluated individually based on the quality of the real estate, the lease structure, tenant operations, and acquisition basis. Building the portfolio one property at a time allowed us to remain selective while assembling a diversified portfolio designed to generate durable cash flow."

Following the closing of Sentinel Opportunity Fund I, the firm will continue focusing on portfolio management while pursuing future investment opportunities consistent with its investment strategy.

About Sentinel Net Lease

Sentinel Net Lease is a private real estate investment manager specializing in single-tenant net lease investments throughout the United States. The firm acquires and manages office, industrial, and select retail properties using a real estate-focused underwriting approach centered on acquisition basis, asset quality, lease structure, and tenant operations.

data.title: Eurozone Consumer Sentiment Climbs to Highest Level Since February
data.description:
By Ed Frankl 




  Consumer sentiment in the eurozone unexpectedly edged higher for the fourth straight month in August, as the economy continues to show robust growth despite the energy-price shock from the Iran war. 



  The European Commission's flash eurozone consumer-confidence indicator published Friday rose to minus 15.5 from minus 15.9 in July. A consensus of economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected it to fall a little to minus 16.2. 



  Despite the improving trend in recent months, consumer confidence hasn't yet recovered to the minus 12.4 of February before the outbreak of the conflict in the Middle East. The index remains below its long-term average, the commission said. 



  However, the rise in consumer sentiment tallies with business surveys also published Friday. Business activity accelerated a little this month, according to purchasing managers' index data. The eurozone's economy expanded by 0.4% in the second quarter of the year. 



  There was also an improvement in U.K. consumer confidence, which rose to its brightest level in two years, data published earlier Friday showed.

data.title: TikTok Shop Selects OMIE for Seven-Day Spotlight Campaign Ahead of Back-to-School
data.description:
TikTok Shop Selects OMIE for Seven-Day Spotlight Campaign Ahead of Back-to-School

TikTok Shop Selects OMIE for Seven-Day Spotlight Campaign Ahead of Back-to-School

PR Newswire

SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 21, 2026

Seven-day event will bring exclusive offers, creator content and added visibility to one of TikTok Shop's leading lunch brands

SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OMIE, the award-winning children's brand behind the bestselling OmieBox®, has been selected by TikTok Shop for a seven-day Spotlight campaign taking place August 20–26, 2026, during the height of back-to-school shopping.

TikTok Shop's Spotlight program features category-leading brands during their most important shopping moments of the year. Participating brands are selected based on factors including their performance on TikTok Shop, strategic importance to the platform and investment in the campaign.

Throughout the event, TikTok Shop will provide dedicated resources and high-impact platform support designed to increase brand discovery, engagement and sales. Shoppers can expect a wave of OMIE content from creators, special offers and shoppable videos featuring the brand's colorful lineup of bento boxes and accessories.

"Back to school shopping is all about combining convenience with excitement, and that is exactly what TikTok Shop and OMIE are delivering through this Spotlight brand campaign. OMIE represents the thoughtful,  innovative, category-leading brand this program was designed to elevate. Through shoppable videos, exclusive offers, and dynamic creator content, we are providing a seamless shopping experience that turns lunch prep from a chore into an inspiring and creative moment for parents." -- Lucia Chai, TikTok Shop Head of Household and Kitchen

The campaign follows the July 27 launch of OmieBox® Lite, OMIE's newest bento box designed to make everyday cold lunches feel a little more special. Available initially through TikTok Shop and omielife.com, OmieBox Lite features a built-in slim ice pack, a Smart Strap for utensils and snacks, and a hidden Treasure Pocket™ where parents can tuck a note, sticker or small surprise.

"OmieBox® Lite was made for the everyday act of packing lunch," Yen said. "Even when you can't be there, a thoughtful lunch and a little surprise hidden inside can remind your child that you're thinking about them. We can't wait to see how TikTok creators bring that idea to life."

OMIE has built a highly engaged community on TikTok, where creators share lunch-packing ideas, product demonstrations and candid reviews with families preparing for the school year. During the Spotlight campaign, OMIE will significantly increase its investment in creator partnerships and TikTok Shop advertising, helping amplify shoppable content across the platform.

Shoppers can follow OMIE on TikTok at [@omielifeinc] and visit the brand's TikTok Shop from August 12–18 to discover featured products, creator content and limited-time back-to-school offers.

About OMIE

OMIE creates thoughtful products that make it easier for families to eat well wherever the day takes them. The company was founded by mom and entrepreneur Nancy Yen, who created OmieBox after struggling to pack the warm lunches her young son loved alongside cold fruits and vegetables.

Today, OMIE is best known for OmieBox®, the first insulated bento box designed to pack hot and cold foods together. Its growing product line includes OmieBox UP® for bigger appetites, OmieBox® Lite for everyday cold lunches, and the OMIE EasyScoop™ Plate for toddlers learning to self-feed.

OMIE products are available at omielife.com and through retailers including Amazon, Target, Walmart, Pottery Barn Kids and Nordstrom. Learn more at www.omielife.com.

data.title: U.S. Business Activity Expands in August
data.description:
By Jessica Coacci

U.S. business activity in the private sector continued to expand this month, a monthly survey said.

The S&P Global Flash U.S. Composite PMI - based on its surveys of services and manufacturing firms, rose to 56 in August from 54.5 in July. A reading above 50 indicates activity continued to grow.

A surge in service sector business activity helped offset a marked slowing of growth in the manufacturing sector, the latter blamed in part on reduced inventory building and supply delays, the survey said.

"U.S. business is booming, with firms reporting the fastest output growth for over four years so far in the third quarter as the expansion picked up further momentum in August," said Chris Williamson, chief business economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence.

Price pressures meanwhile moderated, especially in terms of selling price inflation. Input cost inflation remained elevated due to higher energy prices, the survey said.
